# infrawrench_saved_filter (Resource)

A named, reusable cost filter that budgets, reports, alerts and dashboard cards can point at by id.

A saved filter has two interchangeable spellings of the same thing: a list of `filter` blocks, and a `query` string. Write **one of them**. They are mutually exclusive on the wire — sending a query alongside a non-empty filter list is a 400 from the server, not a precedence rule the provider can resolve for you.

Whichever one you write, the server returns both: it renders a canonical `query` from filters and parses `filters` back out of a query. That is why `query` is optional *and* computed, and why the `filter` blocks you read back may be ones the server derived rather than ones you wrote.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Display name, 1–120 characters.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Free text explaining what the filter selects. At most 2000 characters.
- `filter` (Block List) Filter clauses, ANDed together. Leave these out if you set `query` instead; the server will parse the query into clauses and return them here. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--filter))
- `query` (String) The filter written as a cost query string, e.g. `provider in (aws, gcp) and service not in (Tax)`.

Set this **or** `filter` blocks, never both. If you leave it unset the server renders it from the `filter` blocks and it becomes a computed, read-only value.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Server-assigned saved filter id. Use it with `terraform import`.

<a id="nestedblock--filter"></a>
### Nested Schema for `filter`

Required:

- `dimension` (String) Cost dimension to filter on. One of `provider`, `account`, `service`, `region`, `resource`, `tag`, `charge_type`, `commitment`.
- `op` (String) `in` to keep matching rows, `not_in` to exclude them.
- `values` (List of String) Values to match. Must not be empty.

Optional:

- `tag_key` (String) Tag key, required when `dimension` is `tag` and rejected otherwise.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The id is in the URL when you open the object in the app, and in the
# --json output of the Infrawrench CLI.
terraform import infrawrench_saved_filter.example 2c3d4e5f-6a7b-8c9d-0e1f-2a3b4c5d6e7f
```
